questions.stem: Why can a person with myopia not see distant objects clearly?

options.text: The lens is too thin to refract light
Light is focused behind the retina
The pupil cannot dilate enough to let light in
Light is focused in front of the retina because the eyeball is too long

questions.explanation: In myopia, the eyeball is too long or the lens is too curved, causing light from distant objects to be focused in front of the retina rather than on it, resulting in a blurred image.
